# 1 Samuel Chapter 2 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 151–153 | **Source Image:** 1SA_002_page_001.jpg, 1SA_002_page_002.jpg, 1SA_002_page_003.jpg

---

**1** And Hannah prayed and said, "My heart exults in the LORD; my horn is exalted in the LORD. My mouth is opened wide against my enemies, for I rejoice in your salvation.

**2** There is none holy like the LORD, for there is none besides you, and there is no rock like our God.

**3** Do not multiply your speaking so very proudly; let not arrogance come from your mouth, for the LORD is a God of knowledge, and by him deeds are weighed.

**4** The bows of the mighty are broken, and those who stumbled are girded with strength.

**5** Those who were full have hired themselves out for bread, and those who were hungry have ceased. Even the barren has borne seven, and she who has many children languishes.

**6** The LORD kills and brings to life; he brings down to Sheol and raises up.

**7** The LORD makes poor and makes rich; he brings low and also exalts.

**8** He raises the poor from the dust; he lifts the needy from the ash heap, to make them sit with princes and inherit a seat of honour. For the pillars of the earth are the LORD's, and he has set the world upon them.

**9** He guards the feet of his faithful ones, but the wicked shall be silenced in darkness, for not by strength shall a man prevail.

**10** Those who contend with the LORD shall be shattered; against them he will thunder in the heavens. The LORD will judge the ends of the earth; he will give strength to his king and exalt the horn of his anointed."

**11** And Elkanah went to Ramah, to his house. And the boy was ministering to the LORD in the presence of Eli the priest.

**12** Now the sons of Eli were worthless men; they did not know the LORD.

**13** And the custom of the priests with the people was this: when any man offered a sacrifice, the priest's servant would come while the meat was boiling, with a three-pronged fork in his hand,

**14** and he would thrust it into the pan, or kettle, or cauldron, or pot. All that the fork brought up, the priest would take for himself. So they did at Shiloh to all the Israelites who came there.

**15** Moreover, before the fat was burned, the priest's servant would come and say to the man who was sacrificing, "Give meat for the priest to roast, for he will not accept boiled meat from you, but only raw."

**16** And if the man said to him, "Let them first burn the fat, and then take as much as your soul desires," then he would say, "No! You shall give it now, and if not, I will take it by force."

**17** And the sin of the young men was very great before the LORD, for the men treated the offering of the LORD with contempt.

**18** And Samuel was ministering before the LORD, a boy wearing a linen ephod.

**19** And his mother would make for him a little robe and bring it up to him year by year when she came up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice.

**20** And Eli would bless Elkanah and his wife and say, "May the LORD give you offspring from this woman in place of the one she has lent to the LORD." And they would go to their home.

**21** Indeed the LORD visited Hannah, and she conceived and bore three sons and two daughters. And the boy Samuel grew up in the presence of the LORD.

**22** Now Eli was very old, and he heard all that his sons were doing to all Israel, and how they lay with the women who were serving at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

**23** And he said to them, "Why do you do such things? For I hear of your evil dealings from all this people.

**24** No, my sons; for it is not a good report that I hear the people of the LORD spreading.

**25** If a man sins against a man, God will mediate for him, but if a man sins against the LORD, who will intercede for him?" But they would not listen to the voice of their father, for the LORD desired to put them to death.

**26** And the boy Samuel continued to grow both in stature and in favour with the LORD and also with men.

**27** And a man of God came to Eli and said to him, "Thus says the LORD: 'Did I indeed reveal myself to the house of your father when they were in Egypt, subject to the house of Pharaoh?

**28** And I chose him out of all the tribes of Israel to be my priest, to go up to my altar, to burn incense, to wear an ephod before me. And I gave to the house of your father all the offerings by fire of the people of Israel.

**29** Why do you kick at my sacrifice and my offering that I have commanded in my dwelling, and honour your sons above me, by fattening yourselves on the choicest of every offering of my people Israel?'

**30** Therefore the LORD, the God of Israel, declares: 'I indeed said that your house and the house of your father should walk before me forever,' but now the LORD declares: 'Far be it from me, for those who honour me I will honour, and those who despise me shall be lightly esteemed.

**31** Behold, the days are coming when I will cut off your arm and the arm of your father's house, so that there will not be an old man in your house.

**32** And you shall look upon the distress of my dwelling in all the good that shall be done to Israel, and there shall not be an old man in your house forever.

**33** And the man of yours whom I shall not cut off from my altar — it shall be to consume his eyes and to grieve his soul, and all the increase of your house shall die as men.

**34** And this shall be the sign to you that shall come upon your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas: in one day they shall both die.

**35** And I will raise up for myself a faithful priest who shall do according to what is in my heart and in my soul. And I will build for him an enduring house, and he shall walk before my anointed forever.

**36** And it shall come to pass that everyone who is left in your house shall come and bow down to him for a piece of silver and a loaf of bread, and shall say, "Please appoint me to one of the priestly offices, that I may eat a morsel of bread."'"

---

## LOGOS Translation Notes

1. **"My horn is exalted"** (v. 1): Hebrew קַרְנִי — the horn as a metaphor for strength and dignity. Hannah's song opens with this image of divinely granted power, anticipating the "horn of his anointed" in v. 10.

2. **"Worthless men"** (v. 12): Hebrew בְּנֵי בְלִיָּעַל — literally "sons of Belial/worthlessness." This is a fixed expression denoting moral depravity, not merely low social standing. The term recurs throughout Samuel as a marker of covenant-breaking character.

3. **"Treated the offering of the LORD with contempt"** (v. 17): Hebrew נִאֲצוּ — a strong verb meaning to spurn or show contempt. The gravity of the priestly sin is theological: they despised the LORD's own sacrificial system.

4. **"Linen ephod"** (v. 18): Hebrew אֵפוֹד בָּד — Samuel, though not of Aaronic descent, serves in priestly garb. The linen ephod marks sacred service; the same garment David will later wear before the Ark (2 Sam 6:14).

5. **"The LORD desired to put them to death"** (v. 25): Hebrew כִּי חָפֵץ יְהוָה לַהֲמִיתָם. The verb חָפֵץ (to delight in, to desire) is rendered formally. This theological statement attributes their judicial hardening to divine purpose.

6. **"Cut off your arm"** (v. 31): Hebrew וְגָדַעְתִּי אֶת זְרֹעֲךָ — "arm" (zeroa) symbolizes strength and power. The prophecy announces the end of priestly authority for Eli's line.

7. **"Faithful priest"** (v. 35): Hebrew כֹּהֵן נֶאֱמָן — from the root אמן (to be firm, reliable). This oracle points forward in the narrative, creating anticipation for Samuel's rise and ultimately for the Zadokite priesthood.

8. **Consistent terms**: "the LORD" for יהוה; "soul" for נֶפֶשׁ (vv. 16, 33, 35); "anointed" for מָשִׁיחַ (vv. 10, 35) — the first occurrence of this theologically charged term in Samuel.

--- LOGOS
